task: Should the box fall, make your very next move the one that picks it back up. If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands.

calls.candidate: hard Existence(at_exit), hard Precedence(holding_box, at_exit), hard Response(box_fell, holding_box)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: Two clauses mistranslate the task. (1) The task says 'make your very next move the one that picks it back up' — 'very next' requires ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) hard, but the candidate uses Response(box_fell, holding_box), which only asks for holding_box at some later step and drops the immediate timing. (2) 'If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands' states a condition at the exit moment; the correct clause is Response(at_exit, holding_box) hard (at_exit is a last-step-only condition, so this demands holding_box on that step). The candidate instead has Precedence(holding_box, at_exit), which only forbids at_exit before the first holding_box — since holding_box is true from step 1, that ban is vacuous and the clause does not require the box at the exit, so it is an added order that fails to capture the stated requirement. Keep the hard Existence(at_exit) (the task is to reach the exit); replace the other two clauses with ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) and Response(at_exit, holding_box), both hard.
